ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 27 May 2020 and the Law of 5 December 2022; Law of 13 January 2019 on the establishment of a Register of Beneficial Owners, as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 April 2019 implementing the UBO register; CSSF Regulation of 14 September 2012, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Extract from the Trade and Companies Register (RCS) of the ultimate parent entity (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) Luxembourg or competent foreign companies registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the HCCH 1961 Convention, followed by notarized legalization of signature if origin is non-Contracting State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Copy of valid passport or national identity card of each UBO and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or police/consular authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by a Luxembourg notary; if issued by non-EU state with no bilateral waiver, apostille from competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from the beneficial ownership register of the ultimate parent company (foreign UBO extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign UBO registry / commercial register in the parent's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization at the Embassy or Consulate of Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or domiciliation agreement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Luxembourg domiciliation provider or lessor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the provider/lessor; apostille not required for domestic Luxembourg documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (judicial record / non-liquidation) from the home registry of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry in the foreign shareholder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; translation into French or German by a sworn translator if in foreign language

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Obliged entities must conduct mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and beneficial owners against the European Union consolidated list of persons subject to financial sanctions, the United Nations Security Council sanctions framework, and the Luxembourg national asset-freeze list (Ministère des Affaires étrangères). Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) screening is required using reliable electronic sources (e.g., World-Check, Dow Jones) with enhanced due diligence triggered for PEPs, their family members, and close associates. If the payment rails include US processors (Stripe/PayPal), additional screening against the OFAC SDN List is applied as a contractual and practical condition.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) web portal via www.lbr.lu (e-filing and name availability search)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be drafted in French, German, or Luxembourgish; names in other languages are admissible only with a sworn transliteration that does not conflict with Luxembourg public order or existing registered names. The RCS requires the name to be distinctive, non-misleading, and capable of display in Latin characters.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may refile a new name request via the LBR portal. If the applicant contests the refusal, a written administrative appeal must be lodged with the Minister of Justice through the Registration Registrar within fifteen days; alternatively, a direct action may be brought before the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within three months of notification. Any name-approved reservation can be renewed for an additional 30-day period by written request to the RCS before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or P.O. box cannot fulfill the statutory registered-office requirement. However, a supervised commercial domiciliation company licensed by the Ministry of Justice under the Law of 15 December 2020 may be engaged to provide registered-office facilities and administrative substance. The domiciliation provider must maintain a physical Luxembourg address and keep corporate records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first two years, rising to 40% if the registered office is a commercial domiciliation facility and the company lacks demonstrable local operational substance. Social security and tax authorities also conduct targeted checks.

Notarial drawing and certification of the articles of incorporation (statuts) and UBO declarations before a Luxembourg notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff and market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company incorporation filing with the RCS and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
UBO register filing (RBE declaration) for the SARL

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC dossier preparation, UBO identification, PEP and sanctions screening (World-Check/Dow Jones and OFAC checks)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML counsel / compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for low-risk standard manufacturing entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/consular legalization for passport and corporate document copies (per document, 5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministère des Affaires étrangères et européennes / Embassy or Consulate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales — Articles 710-1 to 710-25 (SARL), Articles 710-26 et seq. (governance) and Articles 1, 9 and 12 (public order); Loi du 19 décembre 2002 relative au registre du commerce et des sociétés (Arts. 10-11); Loi du 13 janvier 2019 portant création du Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs; relevant RCS/RESA regulations under the Loi du 11 janvier 2008 on electronic filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); electronic filing window: guichet.lu (notary-assisted filing accepted pursuant to the Loi du 11 janvier 2008).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (Deed of Incorporation) — an authentic notarial deed containing the articles of association and the first corporate acts; filed with the RCS and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum statutory capital EUR 12,000 for an SARL; at least 20% of each share (EUR 2,400) must be paid up at subscription, with full payment required within five years. The contribution must be held on a blocked corporate account in the name of the company in formation at a Luxembourg credit institution; the bank's capital-blocking certificate must be remitted to the notary as a condition of signing the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — Pursuant to the articles of incorporation, executed on [date], the founding shareholder resolves as follows: 1. The subscription of the entire share capital, as itemised in the deed, is approved and the bank's capital blocking certificate is acknowledged. 2. The registered office is fixed at [address], L-Luxembourg, constituting the statutory seat and administrative centre for all corporate, tax and regulatory purposes. 3. The following managers are appointed: [name and nationality], acting severally, with full powers of administration, banking and representation. 4. The managers are authorised to complete the RCS filing, RESA publication, establishment-authorisation application, and registration in the RBE. 5. All corporate-governance formalities shall conform to Article 710-1 et seq. of the amended Law of 10 August 1915.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name reservation and legal review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS name-index search and reservation window via guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a free availability search in the RCS name database and file an online name-reservation request with the exact corporate name of the future SARL. Verify compliance with Article 28 of the amended Law of 10 August 1915 (company name must permit clear identification and must not be misleading) and confirm that the same name will be used identically in the notarial deed and in all RCS and RESA filings.
required_dossiers: Certified true copy of officers' ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS refuses or queries the proposed denomination, file a corrected reservation within 15 calendar days adding a distinguishing element (e.g., a registrable suffix); the original filing sequence is preserved where correction is made within the statutory window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital account and bank KYC/AML clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (authorised bank) selected by the founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate account labelled 'SARL en formation' through the founding shareholders or managers-elect; the subscribers transfer the minimum paid-in capital (at least EUR 2,400); the bank will perform KYC/AML review under the Law of 12 November 2004 and issue a capital-blocking certificate (certificat de blocage) addressed to the notary, which must be valid at the signing date.
required_dossiers: Certified passport or ID of each natural shareholder/manager
Proof of residence issued within 3 months
Projected business plan for dice manufacturing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the bank issues a negative KYC decision or requests further clarification, supply additional source-of-wealth evidence or choose another regulated Luxembourg bank; the notary will not sign the deed without a current blocking certificate from at least one approved institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the authentic deed of incorporation before a Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) competent for the planned registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary reviews the draft articles (corporate purpose: manufacture and sale of polymer/moulded hobby dice, ISIC 3240), verifies the legality of the managers' appointments and the capital certificate, reads the deed aloud and signs a single authentic original in the presence of all founding shareholders or by registered notarial proxy; the deed contains the pro-forma first board resolution set out above.
required_dossiers: Criminal-record extract of each manager (casier judiciaire)
Notarial power of attorney where a party is absent
Identity documents of all natural shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For any query by the notary or the RCS, amend the articles by supplementary deed and re-sign before the same notary; the corrected dossier must be refiled within the regulator's response deadline to preserve the registration date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic RCS filing and statutory registration of the SARL
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed and the statutory RCS forms through guichet.lu (typically filed by the notary or authorised agent). The filing must state the registered office, the managers and their powers, the corporate purpose and the subscribed capital. The EUR 75 RCS inscription fee and applicable annex fees are paid; the company acquires legal personality upon registration and assumes the acts performed in its formation from that moment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The RCS will issue a defect letter (régularisation) for missing or non-compliant annexes; cure within 15 working days by substituted filing through the notary; failure to cure leads to a refusal with limited retroactivity, requiring a fresh filing and a new deed if the defect is substantive.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the deed in the RESA and third-party enforceability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — RESA publication office (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the LBR transmits the excerpts to RESA; the deed and the RCS-formatted abstract are published within five working days. The publication is opposable to third parties under the amended Law of 10 August 1915 and activates the limitation periods for actions against the founders; the published excerpt serves as proof for opening bank accounts and entering into commercial leases.
required_dossiers: Standard RESA form with managers' details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA rejects the abstract for formal defects, resubmit a corrected abstract using the RCS electronic interface; the third-party effect will commence only upon valid publication, so a rapid correction is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RBE beneficial-owner declaration and internal governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) — Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of registration, file the RBE declaration identifying the natural person(s) owning or controlling more than 25% of the capital or voting rights. Simultaneously establish the statutory registers: shareholders register, minutes book, RCS-management records and the first meeting file; these are kept at the registered office and are accessible to the registered auditor and tax authorities.
required_dossiers: First annual meeting minutes (or written consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE declaration is returned for correction, re-file within the remaining legal deadline; late or incorrect declarations are penalised under the Law of 13 January 2019 (criminal fine up to EUR 1,250 and publication of the sanction), so a re-filing within 48 hours is recommended.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie — Direction générale des classes moyennes (issuing the establishment authorisation) and, for the physical workshop, the Administration de l'Environnement (classement des établissements) and the competent Commune (urban and building authorisations).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Authorisation) granted under the amended Loi du 2 septembre 2011; where the epoxy-casting workshop is classified, an environmental operating authorisation / classed-establishment permit under the Loi du 21 mars 2017.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (national environmental protection agency), acting with the Commune's building authority for the integrated EIA/urban screening.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category IV — registration/notification (régime de déclaration) for small-capacity resin casting workshops; a full EIA report (classes 1–3) is not expected at this production scale, but the administration may order an EIA screening where VOC load, resin quantities or receiving-environment sensitivity exceed the classed thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to public sewer: pH 6.5–9.5, COD < 2000 mg/L, suspended solids < 1000 mg/L; VOC and solvent emissions compliant with Directive 2004/42/EC and the national VOC implementing decree; solid and liquid epoxy waste stored in labelled, closed containers and removed by licensed waste collectors with transfer-slip documentation under the Loi du 21 mars 2017.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for the workshop, structural load and building-code approval from the Commune (autorisation de bâtir), and occupational safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including local exhaust ventilation for epoxy resin vapours, personal protective equipment protocols and lightning/electrical safety once material electrical loads are installed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Direct Tax Administration (corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) - Indirect Tax and Registration Administration (VAT). Digital portals: MyGuichet.lu (national e-government portal), guichet.lu (business formalities), AEDT eTVA and eCDF filing platforms.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign parent establishing a Luxembourg SARL must: (1) incorporate the SARL before a Luxembourg notary and obtain immediate registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), which automatically issues the 16-digit national number (numero de matricule) used as the corporate tax identification number for CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; (2) file the statutory VAT registration package with the AEDT, either via MyGuichet.lu or the eTVA portal, submitting the certified articles of association, an extract from the foreign trade register (legalized/apostilled and translated where required), a power of attorney, and the appointment of a local VAT representative where the parent is established outside the EU/EEA; (3) receive the VAT identification number (numero d'identification a la TVA) in the format LU + 8 digits, issued within weeks of filing; (4) register for municipal business tax with the commune of the registered office; and (5) apply for an EORI number for customs and export transactions where goods (e.g., polyhedral dice) will be physically exported outside the EU. Non-EU entities may be required to appoint a VAT fiscal representative; EU-established entities may use the EU OSS scheme instead of a national VAT registration for distance sales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the SARL is a resident, non-transparent company taxed at entity level: corporate income tax 15% plus 5% unemployment solidarity surcharge (effective 15.75%), municipal business tax (6.75% in Luxembourg-City, up to 10.5% in other communes), and net wealth tax (0.5% of taxable net wealth above the EUR 500,000 exemption). Worldwide income is taxable in Luxembourg with credit or exemption relief under tax treaties and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; no territorial or pass-through election is available to a SARL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists in Luxembourg; the available statutory elections and regimes are: (i) fiscal unity (tax consolidation) election - a resident SARL held at least 95% by a Luxembourg resident parent (or EU/EEA resident with a Luxembourg permanent establishment) may elect with its parent for integrated taxation for CIT and municipal business tax purposes; (ii) VAT group election (assujetti unique) - allows a 'one-taxpayer' grouping of closely linked Luxembourg entities for VAT neutrality; (iii) EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) and Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) elections - allow non-established e-commerce suppliers (Kickstarter, Stripe, PayPal channel) to declare distance sales and low-value imports without separate national VAT registrations; (iv) the participation exemption regime - applies automatically upon satisfaction of statutory conditions (holding of at least 10% or an acquisition price of EUR 1.2 million, plus subject-to-tax and standard-tax requirements) and can be disapplied only by election; (v) ATAD and hybrid-mismatch elections to apply substitute rules and the CFC regime; (vi) the small-business VAT exemption election (Article 57 of the VAT Law) for annual turnover not exceeding EUR 30,000.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutee (TVA), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis threshold for Luxembourg-established taxable persons: a SARL must register from its first taxable transaction. Small-business exemption: annual turnover not exceeding EUR 30,000 (excluding VAT) under Article 57 of the VAT Law. Non-established suppliers have no threshold - registration, reverse charge, or an OSS solution is due on the first taxable supply in Luxembourg. Intra-Community distance sales of goods to Luxembourg final consumers trigger Luxembourg VAT registration if the EUR 10,000 annual threshold for EU-wide distance sales is exceeded, unless the OSS scheme is elected.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2G electronic invoicing for supplies to Luxembourg public-sector buyers via the national e-invoicing platform (based on PEPPOL and European standard EN 16931), transposing Directive 2014/55/EU. No general B2B e-invoicing mandate and no real-time fiscal clearance mechanism, digital stamping, or SAF-T pre-clearance regime is currently in force in Luxembourg. VAT invoices may be issued electronically (EDI or advanced/qualified electronic signature) provided the authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility are guaranteed; invoices and supporting export documents must be retained for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Article 58 of the Luxembourg VAT Law applies when: (a) goods (e.g., epoxy-resin polyhedral dice) are physically exported from Luxembourg outside the EU customs territory, evidenced by an electronic customs export declaration and transport documentation, with the exporter holding an EORI number; (b) goods are dispatched to a VAT-registered customer in another EU Member State (intra-Community supply) provided the customer's valid VAT identification number is quoted in the invoice, the EC Sales List (ECSL) is filed, and the goods physically leave Luxembourg; (c) ancillary services directly linked to the export or import of goods (freight, handling, customs clearance) are supplied to non-established taxable persons; and (d) distance sales to non-EU private individuals qualify as export supplies if shipped directly outside the EU without clearance for free circulation within the EU. The zero-rated supply must be identified on the invoice with the 'EU 0%' / 'E 0%' code, the export customs declaration number, and the destination country.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Luxembourg/EU Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document) generated via the CELDEC electronic customs clearance system, showing the exporter as declarant and the goods leaving the EU
Transport evidence - Bill of Lading (sea), Air Waybill (air), CMR waybill (road), or postal/express carrier receipt evidencing physical dispatch from Luxembourg to the non-EU destination
Commercial invoice with Incoterms and export terms, referencing the customs declaration and the zero-rating basis

Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing the incoming foreign-currency settlement of the export invoice (required for the export audit trail and for substantiating payments from Kickstarter backers, Stripe, and PayPal proceeds)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities (AEDT) may scrutinise export substantiation within the general 5-year assessment period (extended to 10 years in cases of fraud). If zero-rating is unsupported, the AEDT retrospectively re-assesses VAT at the 17% standard rate (or applicable reduced rate) on the export consideration, applies default interest of 0.8% per commenced month, and imposes administrative fines up to 10% of the underpaid VAT for material errors and up to 100% for deliberate misstatement. Serious VAT evasion involving falsified customs or export paperwork attracts criminal penalties (imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 250,000), joint and several liability of managers and directors, public disclosure, and denial or clawback of previously credited input VAT and refund claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem alongside the European Central Bank (ECB); bank prudential supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). BCL operates TARGET2/TIPS payment settlement, collects balance-of-payments statistics, and implements ECB monetary policy. No standalone Foreign Exchange Administration exists; exchange transactions are subject only to EU capital-movement freedoms (TFEU Articles 63-66) and CSSF AML supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro (EUR) is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls, no counterparty limits, and no central-bank approval for trade, capital injection, dividend, or royalty payments. Profit remittance is unrestricted for a Luxembourg SARL, subject only to the corporate-law solvency test (Law of 10 August 1915, Article 710-11) and dividend withholding tax (15% statutory; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the parent holds at least 10% of capital with the required holding period, or under applicable double-tax treaties). Inbound and outbound EUR transfers settle in real time via TARGET2; the SARL's statutory minimum capital is EUR 12,000 (fully subscribed, at least 25% paid up at constitution, i.e., EUR 3,000), with the paid-in portion blocked in a Luxembourg bank account until RCS registration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg has no export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export receipts. Exporters may hold USD, EUR, or any other currency freely. The BCL only requires threshold-based statistical reporting for balance-of-payments compilation (direct investment positions and external transactions), which the SARL will satisfy through its quarterly/annual BCL forms; no M/T (mandatory conversion) obligations exist within the Eurozone.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: HIGH as a supplementary payment channel; LOW as a replacement for the primary banking relationship. CSSF-authorised or EU-passported Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under PSD2 (e.g., Wise Europe, Revolut, Monese) can provide multi-currency IBANs, automated Stripe/PayPal payouts, and retail FX conversion without a physical Luxembourg branch. However, an EMI cannot hold the statutory blocked share-capital deposit, issue the notary's attestation de blocage, open a documentary letter of credit, or execute an ISDA-derivative hedging line. Recommended structure: use a licensed Luxembourg bank (BGL BNP Paribas or BIL) for capital escrow, outbound trade settlement, and FX hedging; use an EMI or the Stripe/PayPal multi-currency wallet as a collection float for Kickstarter proceeds, sweeping balances daily to the main EUR operational account to minimise counterparty and fragmentation risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is effectively mandatory for at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner during the initial onboarding at traditional Luxembourg banks, as required by the AML Law of 12 November 2004, CSSF Regulation 12-02, and standard bank KYC policies. BGL BNP Paribas, BIL, and BCEE generally require a face-to-face interview in Luxembourg before activating corporate accounts for a newly formed SARL. Remote video-identification is permitted only where the bank maintains a CSSF-accepted digital onboarding procedure (e.g., BIL's digital pilot), and a newly incorporated eurozone SARL funded by a Kickstarter campaign is typically still escalated to an in-person meeting for the first signature card. Practical plan: the founding manager should travel to Luxembourg for 2-3 days, notarize the articles of association, open and fund the capital escrow account, and attend the on-site KYC/economic-purpose interview before the operational account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crowdfunding-derived revenue base: large inbound EUR/USD volumes from Kickstarter (via Stripe Ireland/UK) and PayPal into a brand-new SARL account before any historical financial statements exist.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the live Kickstarter campaign page and backer count proof; Stripe and PayPal settlement reports; the merchant-of-record agreement in the SARL's name; a documented refund and complaint policy; a detailed business plan with product cost sheets for epoxy resin, polyurethane, sharp-edge molds, and packaging; a certified AML risk assessment confirming the product is a tangible, low-risk tabletop gaming accessory (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident and third-country ultimate beneficial owners (e.g., US or Asian shareholders) combined with a foreign manager, triggering enhanced due diligence and possible RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) mismatch or sanctions-list hits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarised and apostilled passports plus police clearance certificates for each director/UBO; 24 months of shareholder bank statements evidencing source of wealth; a signed source-of-funds declaration for the EUR 12,000 capital injection; the complete corporate ownership chain including intermediate holding vehicles; the Luxembourg RBE extract filed within one month of incorporation; tax residency certificates; prior-bank reference letters; and PEP/reputation-risk self-certification if any.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual expected transaction pattern: post-campaign wire spikes from thousands of micro-backers followed by rapid outbound disbursements to suppliers in China and the EU for resin, molds, and packaging, which can be misread as trade-based money laundering or invoice-remittance mismatch.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a pre-authorised transaction file: a rolling 12-month liquidity forecast; documentary evidence for each procurement order (contracts, proforma invoices, MT103/LC or SEPA records); customs declarations (CN23 and export invoices) matching consignment sizes; a commercial justification for the fully wholesale-to-consumer margin; and an internal transaction-monitoring protocol with an audit trail compliant with CSSF Regulation 12-02.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The founding shareholder wires the SARL's initial capital (EUR 12,000 minimum for a standard SARL; at least EUR 3,000 paid up) via SWIFT MT103 from the home bank, citing the ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (equity-linked instruments) or the BCL balance-of-payments statistical code for direct-investment equity capital. The receiving Luxembourg bank requires: (i) the draft notarial deed or executed articles of incorporation; (ii) the shareholder's subscription resolution; (iii) source-of-funds evidence; and (iv) the BCL statistical registration reference; the bank then issues the attestation de blocage (capital blocking certificate) which the notary files with the Luxembourg RCS. For post-incorporation capital increases, repeat the same SWIFT MT103 purpose code and file the notarial amendment at the RCS. Kickstarter/Stripe and PayPal campaign proceeds are routed to the SARL's EUR operational account via SEPA/wire from Stripe Ireland or PayPal Luxembourg/UK; USD payouts are either held in a USD sub-account or converted to EUR at the processor's or the bank's standing FX rate. Verification of each receipt is evidenced by MT103 / pain.001 transaction details and Stripe's weekly settlement reports.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail for EU/EEA suppliers (epoxy resin, silicone molds, pigments, packaging) is SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001) or SEPA Instant, with ISO purpose code 'TRAD' or 'SUPP', settling in T+1 (or seconds for instant). For non-EU suppliers in China and the US (sharp-edge dies, custom silicone molds, bulk resin batches), use SWIFT MT103 with GPI tracking, including invoice numbers, INCOTERM references (EXW/FOB/DAP), and the trade-contract number. Documentary transactions for large campaign preorders are handled through an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700 under UCP600 by the Luxembourg bank. PayPal and Stripe payouts are consolidated via processor payout files into the SARL's EUR IBAN. All disbursements above EUR 10,000 should be pre-uploaded as a transaction expectation list so the bank's AML engine has the full audit trail; underlying commercial contracts and freight documents must be retained and matched to each wire to satisfy CSSF 12-02 review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forward contracts executed directly with the Luxembourg bank under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement (non-financial counterparty exemption below EMIR clearing thresholds).
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) covering the mismatch between USD-denominated Kickstarter receivables and EUR-denominated operating expenses.
FX vanilla options (caps, collars, put/call spreads) for booking flexibility with paid premiums, requiring a MiFID II-licensed counterparty.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for hedging non-convertible settlement currencies such as CNY/CNH or KRW, permitted solely for economic hedging of Asian supplier payables.

Processor-native FX conversion via Stripe/PayPal for small contestable amounts, limited to spot conversion with transparent margin disclosure; all derivative hedging must be executed through the licensed credit institution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes) submitted through the eCDF electronic filing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 10,000 imposed by the RCS; repeated failure to file may lead to judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off of the SARL

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting (AGM) held and minutes recorded in the corporate minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with a regulator; retained in the company's statutory minute book and available for RCS inspection upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may incur civil liability for failure to call the AGM; no direct RCS strike-off, but persistent default accompanies non-filing of annual accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and net wealth tax returns (to be filed in conjunction with the financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by 31 May following the fiscal year, or within the extended official notice period for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax, monthly interest accrual on overdue tax, coercive collection procedures, and potential director liability; no direct strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual verification of the register of beneficial owners and, where relevant, update of the RBE declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; no standalone annual filing, but the register must be audited and confirmed during the annual meeting cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 and criminal penalties up to EUR 1.25 million for persistent non-disclosure; non-compliance may also impede banking and commercial operations

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is required if the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, and average workforce above 50 employees during the financial year
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial and company register and annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for certain entities and may be required for public-interest entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must keep a current beneficial ownership register and file changes with the RBE within 30 days. There is no separate annual UBO return, but the board of managers must verify and confirm the accuracy of the UBO register during the annual book-close process and record that confirmation in the minutes of the annual general meeting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000 - 15,000 USD per year when audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City aggregate: 17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption from CIT and municipal business tax on qualifying dividends and capital gains (holding >=10% or acquisition cost >=EUR 6,000,000, minimum 12-month holding). IP Box regime: 80% deduction of net qualifying IP income and related capital gains. R&D tax credit and 20% increased deduction for SME R&D expenditure. Unlimited carryforward of tax losses. Minimum net wealth tax of EUR 535 to EUR 4,815 per annum depending on balance sheet totals. Advance R&D credit refundable for new companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1001 (Declaration d'impot sur le revenu des collectivites) filed electronically via the Luxembourg e-filing portal 'MyGuichet.lu' or the ACD eCDF system; quarterly advance tax payments are made via the e-TVA/bank payment referencing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory filing deadline is 30 September following the fiscal year-end; extension to 31 December is available upon written request to the Administration des contributions directes (ACD). Quarterly advance CIT payments are due 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the opening and closing dates of the reporting period (calendar year or statutory accounting year).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident manufacturer or distributor must align the reporting period with the SARL's statutory accounts; a non-calendar year is accepted if consistently used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Insert the 16-digit Luxembourg business registration number (LBR) and the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Societes) number of the SARL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the exact legal identifier of the Luxembourg entity; foreign shareholder/TAX identification numbers must be presented in an annex, never in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed net commercial profit after book-to-tax adjustments, net operating loss carryover, and deduction of preferential IP Box or 80% IP deduction; split between CIT base, municipal business tax base and solidarity surcharge base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all worldwide turnover realized through Kickstarter, Stripe and PayPal merchant accounts if booked in the Luxembourg SARL; foreign income attributable to a foreign permanent establishment is exempt with progression and must be disclosed in the annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare available prior-year losses and current-year utilization; Luxembourg allows indefinite loss carryforward, subject to the 50% change-of-control safeguard rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a loss carryforward schedule; losses of a foreign shareholder or of a foreign branch not booked in Luxembourg cannot be assumed by the SARL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B - Participation Exemption / IP Box Election (Regime des societes meres / Regime IP)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mark the election for the 100% participation exemption on dividends/capital gains or the 80% IP Box deduction; attach substantiation (shareholding register, holding period, IP tracking schedule).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 12-month holding period and the 10% or EUR 6,000,000 acquisition threshold must be met; non-resident parent details and treaty residence certificate are evidentiary annexes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare quarterly CIT advance payments made (10 March, 10 June, 10 September, 10 December) and any prior-year overpayment credited.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits and withholding tax refund claims (Form 100D) are reported in the annex, not in this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section 11 - Net Wealth Tax Base (Impôt sur la fortune)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net wealth = balance sheet net assets plus hidden reserves, less a EUR 500,000 allowance, taxed at 0.5%; statutory minimum NWT of EUR 535 (assets below EUR 350,000), EUR 1,605 (EUR 350,000-2,000,000) or EUR 4,815 (above EUR 2,000,000).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not subject to Luxembourg net wealth tax on shares of a Luxembourg SARL; complete this box solely on the company's own balance sheet.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 1001 triggers: (i) ex officio default assessment (taxation d'office); (ii) administrative fine between EUR 100 and EUR 5,000 per return; (iii) late-payment interest at 0.6% per month on the unpaid CIT and municipal business tax; (iv) loss of extension privileges and possible criminal prosecution for repeated non-filing. Failure to file the NWT return results in the minimum net wealth tax being assessed plus interest and penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (applied at source by the paying SARL on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU corporate shareholders holding at least 10% for 12 months; treaty-reduced to 5% for substantial holdings or 15% for portfolio holdings, depending on the applicable DTA)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must deliver to the Luxembourg paying agent before the distribution date: (i) a valid foreign Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority; (ii) a completed Form 100D 'Application for reduction or refund of withholding tax'; and (iii) a shareholding statement evidencing the holding percentage and holding period. The Luxembourg ACD (Bureau d'imposition) grants relief-at-source upon approval; if tax was withheld in full, a refund claim must be filed with the ACD within the general limitation period (5 years). For EU resident parent companies satisfying the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, an advance administrative clearance can be obtained via the Luxembourg 'agreement' procedure; otherwise, withholding is applied at 15% and refunded upon documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose domestic withholding tax on outbound royalty or interest payments. Under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive and most Luxembourg tax treaties, the effective rate for qualifying related companies is 0%; arm's length substance, beneficial ownership and anti-abuse conditions apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 700,000,000 (consolidated group revenue at the EU parent level triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation); below this threshold, Luxembourg-headquartered SARLs must nonetheless maintain contemporaneous arm's length documentation and respond to ACD transfer pricing requests within statutory deadlines.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies the OECD anti-abuse doctrine, the ATAD GAAR, and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive anti-abuse clause: an SARL must demonstrate real economic substance (registered office in Luxembourg, physical premises, full-time qualified personnel, local management meetings, substantive assets and risk-taking) to obtain treaty benefits, the participation exemption and the IP Box. Under the proposed EU ATAD 3 'shell entity' directive, Luxembourg-resident companies without minimal substance would be deemed to lack tax residence and would lose access to double tax treaties and EU directive protections; the ACD already applies a substance-over-form analysis in abuse cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - False Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting gross receipts from Kickstarter, Stripe or PayPal merchant accounts, inflating production costs, or understating the taxable profit in Form 1001 of the Luxembourg SARL to reduce or eliminate the 24.94% aggregate corporate tax charge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of evaded CIT plus 0.6% monthly late-payment interest; administrative penalty surcharge of 5%-10% of the under-declared tax; criminal fine of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of one month to five years under Article 426 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law and the Criminal Code; mandatory publication of the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gerant (managing director) is solidarily liable for the evaded tax, late-payment interest and criminal fine; conviction triggers an automatic travel ban, disqualification from managing Luxembourg companies, seizure of personal assets, and imprisonment up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form 1001 by 30 September of the following fiscal year, failure to file the Net Wealth Tax declaration, or failure to pay quarterly CIT advances for the SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ex officio assessment by the ACD based on estimated income; administrative fine of EUR 100 to EUR 5,000 per unfiled return; late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; loss of the ability to claim loss carryforwards in the default assessment for the first year; escalation to tax recovery proceedings and judicial enforcement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gerant bears personal civil liability for the resulting tax deficiency under the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies and faces criminal liability for willful non-filing, including a travel ban and imprisonment up to five years; shareholders may bring a civil damages action against the gerant for mismanagement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Luxembourg SARL is used as a letterbox conduit: it receives treaty-protected dividends, royalties or interest, or benefits from the participation exemption and IP Box, while having no local personnel, no physical premises, no bank account in Luxembourg, and no substance; management decisions are taken entirely from a foreign parent's office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, withdrawal of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption, recharacterization of the arrangement under the GAAR, taxation of deemed distributions at the 24.94% aggregate rate plus late interest and a 5%-10% penalty surcharge; under EU ATAD 3 once finalized, shell entities would be denied tax residence and lose access to double tax treaties; the ACD may also impose minimum net wealth tax at the highest bracket (EUR 4,815).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face personal liability for the tax adjustment; criminal prosecution for breach of fiduciary duty; travel bans; seizure of personal bank accounts; disqualification from acting as director in Luxembourg for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SARL's Kickstarter, Stripe or PayPal merchant accounts to process payments for undisclosed third parties (money laundering 'layering'), accepting cash sales above EUR 10,000 without AML verification/reporting, or knowingly processing proceeds from fraudulent crowdfunding campaigns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the amended AML Law of 12 November 2004, administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for entities; freezing of corporate and merchant accounts by bank and judicial order; supplementary CSSF disciplinary measures; criminal sanctions for money laundering complicity of 5 to 10 years imprisonment and fines up to EUR 250,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficial owners and gerants are personally liable for the AML penalties; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed during the investigation; criminal conviction carries imprisonment and permanent disqualification from commercial activities in Luxembourg.
